pages._note: Allowed: true | false for each page. Which pages the site offers. false removes that page's tab, overview card and pane; a deep link to it falls back to the overview. Overview and Sandbox cannot be hidden: the overview is the fallback, and its prose links to the sandbox mid-sentence.

display._note: How the Simulation 2.5 map draws things. Changes no result. The page reads this on reload; republish too so a copy of the page hosted on its own follows.
display._homes_level: Allowed: "main" | "raised". main: each home sits at the level of the main its connection joins, so connections lie flat, as the utility's own map draws them. raised: each home sits raised_height_m above its main and its connection slopes down to it, which keeps the homes apart from the pipes but, with heights exaggerated x22, turns a 6.7 m connection into a near-vertical stick.
display._raised_height_m: Allowed: a number of metres from 0 to 20. Used only when homes_level is "raised"; about 0.5 to 1 keeps the homes apart from the pipes without the sticks.

pumps._note: Pump stations at a set rate, for growth scenarios only (option A, 14 Oct 2026). The published grid and every placement still use SWMM IDEAL pumps, which pass on whatever reaches the wet well at once (L7). A scenario that switches 'Pump at set rates' on is solved by the local SWMM runner with each station as a wet-well tank and a constant-rate pump that starts and stops on its levels, against a baseline at the default rates; the page's instant estimate cannot model stop-start pumping, so it never does this. None of these values is published by the utility: every one is an assumption until the operator supplies duty points and wet-well levels.
pumps._rising_main_velocity_m_s: Allowed: a velocity in m/s, 0.3 to 3. A station's default rate is this velocity in its rising main's published bore: 7.9 L/s in DN100 and 17.7 L/s in DN150 at 1.0 m/s. A common design figure for self-cleansing rising mains, not a measurement.
pumps._default_rate_lps: Allowed: null, or a rate in L/s, above 0 and up to 200. null derives each station's default from its rising main (above); a number gives every station that rate instead.
pumps._stations: Allowed: {} or { "<rising main id>": rate in L/s, ... }. Fixed defaults for named stations, keyed by the first rising main from the wet well, as the station card shows it: "4433449" (wet well N183, 14 homes, DN150) and "1495438" (wet well N997, 41 homes, DN100). Overrides default_rate_lps and the velocity rule.
pumps._wet_well_area_m2: Allowed: a plan area in m2, 0.5 to 50. About a 1.8 m diameter wet well.
pumps._levels: Allowed: metres above the wet-well floor, stop_level_m below start_level_m. The pump starts when the water reaches start_level_m and stops when it falls to stop_level_m.
pumps._inlet_above_start_m: Allowed: metres, 0 to 2. How far the incoming sewer enters above the start level, so a filling wet well never backs up the pipes that feed it, as wet wells are built. The published node is the incoming pipe's end, so the wet-well floor is put this much plus start_level_m below it.
pumps._curve: Allowed: "head" | "flat". head (since 15 Oct 2026): each pump follows a centrifugal curve, so it delivers less as the level it pumps against rises (the discharge manhole filling, a surcharged trunk) and stops at its shut-off head; the curve passes through the station's rate at the head it needs at that rate: the lift from the wet well's mid level to the discharge manhole, plus rising-main friction at that rate. flat: the rate whatever the head, as before.
pumps._shutoff_head_ratio: Allowed: 1.1 to 3. The shut-off head as a multiple of the rated head: 1.2 to 1.4 is typical of the small centrifugal pumps in sewage stations. Pump curves are not published; this sets the curve's shape.
pumps._rising_main_hazen_c: Allowed: 60 to 160. Hazen-Williams C for rising-main friction (120: a lined or plastic main in service). Lengths and bores are the published rising mains: 46.5 m of DN150 from N183, 228.1 m of DN100 from N997.
pumps._rated_window: A stop-start pump never settles, so a rated run lasts rated_minutes and every depth is the PEAK over its last rated_window_min, which must span at least one whole pump cycle. At default rates N183 cycles about every 80 min at Design wet and 3 h in Dry, N997 every 30 min and 1 h, so 240 holds at least one burst in every case; lower rates or smaller inflows lengthen the cycle. Ideal runs keep the grid's 480 minutes and 10-minute window.
pumps._future: Option B, not done: re-run the whole grid (about 8.5 h) with rated pumps so the published heatmap and placements include them, judging detection on the peak across a pump cycle rather than the settled depth. Worth doing once the operator confirms each station's pump rate, wet-well size and start and stop levels; its SCADA run-hours could then check the model, and rising run-hours are themselves evidence of growth behind a station.

manning_n_by_material._note: Roughness by the published MATERIAL code (H3). Conventional design values from Chow (1959) Table 5-6, the table the SWMM reference reproduces. Used by SWMM in Simulation 2.5, by the sandbox's capacity model, and by the Simulation 2.5 page's growth estimate.

infiltration_weight_by_age._note: P26 / L5: in the age-weighted I&I case, a pipe's infiltration is multiplied by the weight of the first band whose upper construction year it falls under, then all weights are rescaled so total I&I is unchanged. Older pipes leak more. [upper year, weight].

blockage_likelihood._note: The sandbox's blockage-likelihood score (src/model/osp_risk.js, where each value's argument and full references are set out). Weights from the mutual-information ranking of [Ma25] (age 0.124 first, diameter second) and the factor review of [MM20]; [DP22] and [Al23] on small pipes. Not used by Simulation 2.5.

loads._note: How connected properties and new dwellings become flow in Simulation 2.5.
loads._sources: P01 2.81 = 8,023 people / 2,851 connections (ABS 2021); G4 2.3 = ABS 2021 household size; P01b 200 L/person/day (Barwon Water, WSAA supplement s3.2.2); P02 peak 2.0; R9 trough 0.2, the midpoint of 0.10-0.30 x ADF (UW CEE 481).

simulation._note: Simulation 2.5: where growth is tested, how much, and what counts as a sensor seeing it.
simulation._study_area: Allowed: "segment" | "whole". segment: the 71 manholes draining to segment_outlet_node, results in results/sim25/grid. whole: all 328 published manholes in the model domain, results in results/sim25/grid_whole.
simulation._overflow_inlet: Allowed: "published" | "raised". The three overflow (relief) pipes have no recorded direction or inlet height. published (the grid as run): each takes its published inverts, so overflow pipe 4433446, whose inlet is level with its manhole's outlet, carries everyday flow: 70% of what leaves MH4451967 runs back to the N183 wet well, a loop no real station has. raised: each overflow inlet sits at least at the crown of its manhole's main outlet, so it carries water only once the manhole surcharges. Rated pump scenarios always use raised. Switching the grid needs a re-run (option B).
simulation._dwellings: P05: growth sizes added at one manhole, and the stress case; corridor sizes, of which 390 and 485 are the PlanSA 2021-41 medium and high projections.
simulation._alarm_depth_mm: G6: the operator's low alarm, depth above the pipe floor. Stored with every SWMM run, so changing it needs a re-run.
simulation._republish_only: detection_rises_mm and max_sensors are applied to the stored runs by the builder.
simulation._case_set: Allowed: the name of any set under case_sets (as committed, "five" | "all_twelve"). Which of case_sets below is run and published. Each case is one combination of what cannot be measured yet, and costs 1,641 whole-domain SWMM runs (about 87 min on 9 workers) in the whole area.

simulation._case_sets: weather: the nominal sweep, one case each; ii is P04, infiltration in L/s per 100 m of pipe. sensitivity: at_ii names the weather levels that get the variants; each variant overrides fields of a case and adds its label. Allowed fields in a variant's set: pf "flat" | "harmon" (peaking); age "uniform" | "weighted" (I&I by pipe age); bfac a multiplier on outside inflow, such as 0.5 or 1.5; stage metres above the outfall invert, or null for a free outfall; hour "peak" | "trough" of the daily cycle. at_ii may only name ii values listed in weather.
